claims.answer: Electron desktop app for macOS 13+ (Apple Silicon and Intel) and Linux (AppImage and deb, x64 and arm64); native iPhone companion in TestFlight beta that pairs through a relay. No Windows, Android, browser or CLI.

desktop_os.answer: README badge and install section list macOS 13+ (arm64, Intel) and Linux x64/arm64; AI account docs say Windows is not supported yet.

mobile_apps.answer: iPhone companion app (TestFlight beta) with Queue, Flows, History and new chats; no Android app.

cli.answer: package.json has no bin entry and no CLI is documented.

task_actions.answer: Desktop does everything; the phone starts chats, answers questions, allows or denies tool requests, reads plans, starts and stops flows; retry of failed steps is desktop-only.

notifications.answer: Phone alerts when a chat finishes and desktop badges for approvals and questions.

limitations: iPhone app is a beta companion and needs the desktop awake with Frink open.

evidence.title: Frink README
evidence.locator: Features; Supported Agents; Install; Linux; Also in the box
evidence.finding: Desktop app that runs Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot and Cursor side by side (up to four panes, worktrees), Flows with triggers (Linear, Jira, Shortcut, ClickUp, Sentry, PostHog, Vercel, webhook, schedule), a Work Queue, permissions gate, plugins and MCP, own AI sign-in, local SQLite; macOS 13+ and Linux builds, iPhone beta; MIT; official builds send anonymous usage counts and crash reports.

evidence.title: Getting started
evidence.locator: First launch; Connect an AI account; Start your first chat
evidence.finding: Connect an existing Claude, Codex, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot or Cursor login, then start a general or project chat; the matching CLI must be installed and logged in.

evidence.title: AI accounts
evidence.locator: macOS and Linux for now; one sign-in per provider per machine; bundled claude binary
evidence.finding: Frink stores no Claude or Codex token and runs the signed-in account; OpenCode, Copilot and Cursor are macOS and Linux only; Windows is not supported yet; Frink ships its own bundled claude binary.

evidence.title: Task lifecycle
evidence.locator: Task states; Agent-declared states; Stopping a task; Renderer-only recovery
evidence.finding: Task states Pending, Running, Plan Ready, Needs Attention, Ready for review, Completed, Failed, Cancelled and Interrupted; agent completion signals; a question waits about 9.5 minutes; macOS keeps a running task alive after the window closes but quitting stops it.

evidence.title: Flows
evidence.locator: Anatomy of a flow; Project defaults; Flow briefing; Run history
evidence.finding: Visual pipelines with one trigger (manual, webhook, schedule, post-task) plus blocks, run history, flow briefing and custom nodes; Flow steps run on Claude or OpenAI only; agents can patch flows through MCP tools.

evidence.title: Plugins
evidence.locator: Two kinds of plugin; Letting a service tell Frink when something happens; Run your own relay
evidence.finding: Plugins provide chat tools and Flow triggers/actions; events arrive only while Frink is open and online, best effort and not queued; relay is Frink's address or your own via FRINK_WEBHOOK_BASE_URL.

evidence.title: MCP servers
evidence.locator: Where Frink stores MCPs; Credentials: per-machine; Security considerations
evidence.finding: Frink is an MCP client with auto-import of servers, per-project or global servers and per-machine encrypted credentials.

evidence.title: Permissions
evidence.locator: The short version; The three scopes; What's always blocked; Auto permission mode
evidence.finding: Per-tool permission prompts with project, user and managed policy scopes, an always-blocked credential-path list that is a static check not a sandbox, and an Auto mode.

evidence.title: What Frink sends
evidence.locator: Usage counts; Turning usage counts off; Crash reports
evidence.finding: Official builds send anonymous usage counts to PostHog (switch off in Settings, Privacy) and crash reports to Sentry (not switchable); source builds send nothing; update check contacts Frink's download server.

evidence.title: Worktree setup
evidence.locator: Two different .frink paths; Configuring setup commands
evidence.finding: Chats can run in a git worktree under ~/.frink/worktrees with per-project setup commands from .frink/worktrees.json.

evidence.title: Projects and general chat
evidence.finding: A chat has a project folder or is a general chat with no files; projects can be started from scratch, opened or cloned.

evidence.title: Reviewing changes
evidence.finding: Every changed file shows as a diff; the built-in editor and terminal allow fixes; chats can roll back to a checkpoint.

evidence.title: Frink relay
evidence.locator: What it is not; The two secrets
evidence.finding: Small relay that forwards webhook and phone traffic to the desktop app without storing anything; deliveries are dropped when the app is not connected; relay learns the subscribe key.

evidence.title: Frink for iPhone
evidence.locator: Connect your computer; Use and recovery; Alerts
evidence.finding: Native iPhone companion (TestFlight beta): pair by QR through the relay, Queue, Flows, History and starting chats; execution and files stay on the computer, which must stay awake with Frink open.

evidence.title: MIT License
evidence.finding: MIT License, copyright Benji Norval, covering the repository.

evidence.title: Frink package manifest
evidence.finding: Version 0.4.0, MIT; dependencies include the Claude Agent SDK, @sentry/electron, posthog-node, croner and Electron tooling; no bin entry, so no CLI.

evidence.title: Flow admission config
evidence.finding: Flow runs are admitted up to a configurable maxConcurrentRuns with queuing.

evidence.title: Admission store
evidence.finding: Computes free slots from maxConcurrentRuns minus occupied runs; excess runs queue.

evidence.title: Schedule trigger
evidence.finding: Flow schedule triggers use croner cron expressions inside the desktop app.

evidence.title: Webhook listener
evidence.finding: Desktop webhook listener verifies signatures and starts flows from relayed deliveries.

evidence.title: Worktree creation
evidence.locator: git worktree add under git lock (L118, L144)
evidence.finding: Creates a worktree after fetching the base, serialized per project with a git lock.

evidence.title: Flows MCP tools
evidence.finding: Frink exposes frink_flows_* MCP tools so agents can list, read, patch and run flows inside Frink.

evidence.title: Analytics client
evidence.finding: Sends PostHog events including pr_created, gated by the Share Usage Analytics setting.

evidence.title: Privacy switch
evidence.finding: Settings tab holds the Share Usage Analytics switch.

evidence.title: GitHub repository API
evidence.finding: Public repository benord-labs/frink: 177 stars, MIT license, pushed 2026-11-17 (observed 2026-11-17).

evidence.title: Frink 0.4.0 release
evidence.finding: Release 0.4.0 published 2026-10-16 with macOS arm64/x64 DMGs, Linux x64/arm64 AppImages and arm64/amd64 debs.

evidence.title: Bounded search: other clients
evidence.locator: ls src mobile relay; package.json bin; grep -rniE "android|express.*listen|vscode extension" src mobile/app.json
evidence.finding: Only the Electron app, an iPhone app (Android only appears as an audio-permission flag) and the relay exist; package.json has no bin so there is no CLI; no web client or editor extension.

evidence.title: Bounded search: cost and billing
evidence.finding: Cost fields exist only in Claude message types and context-usage code; no per-task cost UI, budget or spend limit.

evidence.title: Bounded search: teams, roles, SSO
evidence.finding: No user accounts, organizations, roles, SSO or presence; the managed policy file is the only admin construct.

evidence.title: Bounded search: remote execution
evidence.finding: ssh and remote matches are git, shell env and MCP transport handling; no remote host, container or VM execution.

evidence.title: Bounded search: specs and memory
evidence.finding: No persistent product spec or memory store; Flow briefing is shared text per flow.

evidence.title: Bounded search: dependencies and limits
evidence.finding: No task dependencies, token or spend limits; flows have edges and admission limits.

evidence.title: Diff panel git handoffs
evidence.locator: DiffPanelHeader DiffHandoffs type (L25-L36) and menu items (L78-L115); active-chat.tsx handoffs (L1918-L1930); builtin-commands.ts pr-comments (L9, L89)
evidence.finding: The diff panel never changes the repo; its Ask agent menu sends the agent a chat message to commit, create a pull request, commit and push to the PR, review changes, fix merge conflicts (when the PR is CONFLICTING) or merge the pull request; a /pr-comments command asks the agent to write PR review comments.

evidence.title: Pull request status through gh
evidence.locator: src/main/lib/git/github/github.ts fetchGitHubPRStatus (L25-L125); trpc routers chats/pr/merge.ts mergePr (L12-L40)
evidence.finding: fetchGitHubPRStatus runs gh pr view for number, state, draft, reviewDecision, mergeable and statusCheckRollup, caches it for 10 seconds and derives a checks status; a mergePr procedure accepts merge, squash or rebase through gh but the diff panel merge action is an agent message.

evidence.title: Settings Usage tab
evidence.finding: Usage history from transcripts: total tokens, busiest day, daily Claude and Codex token totals in a heatmap, streaks, busiest hour, favourite model, conversations, flow runs, tasks finished and top flows; ProviderUsage shows Claude and Codex plan rate-limit windows (five-hour, seven-day, per-model) with reset time and pace. No per-project breakdown, currency cost or export was found.

evidence.title: Attachment images in task prompts
evidence.finding: Trigger-context image attachments are read and converted to base64 for the provider send, and images pasted by the user while resuming a task are appended to the prompt.

evidence.title: Reviewer search: CPU and RAM awareness
evidence.finding: Only src/main/lib/diagnostics/heap-watch.ts, which reads free and total memory for Frink's own heap diagnostics; no CPU or RAM based scheduling or limits.

evidence.title: Reviewer search: ports and services
evidence.finding: No matches; no port allocation, service orchestration or collision handling.

evidence.title: Reviewer search: indexing and retrieval
evidence.finding: Only Cursor permission-gate code that asks Cursor's own ripgrep which files a search walks and an unescaped-path comment; no repository index or retrieval of Frink's own.

evidence.title: Reviewer search: deployments, reverts and commit links
evidence.finding: Matches are the Vercel and Supabase integration descriptions, mobile relay deployment and the vendor plugin pin check; no deployment link, revert or commit link feature.

evidence.title: Reviewer search: data export
evidence.finding: Only MCP OAuth function names; no chat, history or settings export feature.

evidence.title: Reviewer search: telemetry consent prompt
evidence.finding: Only MCP vendor-plugin consent and a Flows batch consent card; no first-run analytics consent prompt, and user-docs/telemetry.md describes only the Share Usage Analytics switch.
